basis: Developmental impairment and epileptic encephalopathy define the disorder; hypotonia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Poikiloderma and congenital neutropenic immune deficiency define disease; nasolacrimal obstruction in 3/3 assessed. Secondary infections do not establish additional organ damage.
Mitochondrial disorder with defining neurodegeneration; retinopathy/optic neuropathy and gastrointestinal dysmotility each reported in 80-99%.
Persistent hyperkeratotic skin papules define this epidermal disorder.
Glycogen storage I subtype with hepatic glycogen accumulation and impaired glucose homeostasis; subtype-specific renal functional damage frequency is unclear.
IgE-mediated allergy; episodic urticaria, gastrointestinal symptoms and anaphylaxis do not establish persistent organ damage.
Chronic inflammation of the ethmoid sinus; infectious, allergic and structural causes vary across patients.
Defined by small-intestinal inflammation; the umbrella does not establish a specific infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Immature teratoma arising within the central nervous system.
Inherited leucine metabolism disorder with many asymptomatic patients; hypotonia and movement abnormalities do not establish lasting neural or muscle damage in >=30%.
Congenital multiple joint contractures define this MYBPC1-related arthrogryposis syndrome.
Carcinoma of the lip, classified here as an oral cavity primary.
Developmental disorder; eczema 2/2 assessed, cataract/high myopia and scoliosis each 1/1. Small denominators limit certainty; PDA 1/1 omitted under cap.
Muscular dystrophy defines the group; skin fragility/blistering occurs in the predominant EBS-with-dystrophy phenotype (>30%), but not isolated limb-girdle disease.
Liver fluke infection directly involves hepatic tissue and the biliary tract; ectopic organ disease is uncommon.
Congenital cleft between the laryngotracheal airway and oesophagus, with severe swallowing dysfunction and pulmonary damage.
Acute periapical periodontal inflammation, usually from infection extending from the dental pulp; noninfectious pulpal causes also occur.
Localized inherited skin blistering and nail dystrophy; generalized mucosal complications are not characteristic of this form.
Neurodegenerative parkinsonism with dementia and neuronal loss; urinary incontinence and dysphagia alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the exocrine pancreas; secondary diabetes is a separately diagnosed disease.
Rhabdoid tumour arising in striated muscle tissue.
Air and blood occupy the pleural cavity and impair lung expansion; pleural bleeding does not itself establish a blood disorder.
Neoplasm located in the epicardium, a component of the heart and visceral pericardium.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; severe thoracic restriction causes respiratory failure/asphyxia in most described neonatal cases.
Neuropathy, deafness and intestinal aganglionosis define PCWH; lacrimal dysfunction in 2/3 assessed. Hypogonadism (30-79%) omitted under cap; pigment changes alone are non-damaging.
